newsitem.title: INDIA: Enron, 13 others to bid for India project.
newsitem.headline: Enron, 13 others to bid for India project.

text.p: Fourteen global firms including Enron Corp of the U.S. are expected to bid for a 120-billion-rupee ($3.35 billion) gas terminal-cum-power plant project in India, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.

The news agency quoted M. Karunanidhi, chief minister of the southern state of Tamil Nadu, as saying on Wednesday that the state would soon invite global bids for the project which would include a liquified natural gas (LNG) terminal, a gasification plant and a 2500 megawatt power plant.
Enron International is an affiliate of Enron Corp.

Karunanidhi said Royal Dutch Shell, Mobil Corp and Japan's Marubeni Corp were among the firms showing an interest in the project to be located in a 7,000-acre petrochemical park at Ennore, a port on the outskirts of Madras, the state capital.
The LNG terminal would handle two million tonnes of imported gas per year and would be supported by a conversion plant for supply to the power plant, PTI said.
Karunanidhi said the park would also house a series of chemical and petrochemical industries.
